h1: Dental Crowns That Look Completely Natural
intro: Most dentistry looks like dentistry. Our goal is to provide dentistry that is completely undetectable.

Dr. Marshall H. Brown uses high-grade porcelain and porcelain-on-gold crowns to restore even the most severely damaged teeth — giving you back a beautiful, fully functional smile that lasts 20 to 30 years.

sections.h2: What Is a Dental Crown? And Do You Need One?
body: A dental crown is a custom-fitted cap that completely encases a damaged, decayed, cracked, or weakened tooth — restoring its shape, strength, appearance, and function. Once cemented in place, a crown looks, feels, and works exactly like a natural tooth.

Where damage to a person's teeth is extreme — and apparently beyond repair — Dr. Brown can use porcelain or porcelain-on-gold crowns to make the smile appear as new. This is an extremely reliable technique for repairing even the most severe dental problems, including permanently replacing missing teeth to offer a complete smile and a functional bite.

These treatments are used for long-lasting correction of major dental problems. It is usual for these restorations to last for 20 to 30 years — which is as close to permanent as dental treatment can get.
bullets: Replaces and restores severely damaged or missing teeth
Completely undetectable — looks and feels like your natural tooth
Supports misshapen, cracked, or badly broken teeth
Fixes functional chewing problems and bite issues
Protects teeth after root canal treatment
Relieves unexplained pain caused by hairline cracks in molars

body: Dr. Brown selects the most appropriate material for your crown based on the location of the tooth, the severity of damage, your bite, and your aesthetic goals. During your consultation, he'll explain exactly which option is best suited to your specific situation.

All-Porcelain Crown (Most Natural Look): Full porcelain crowns offer the most lifelike appearance and are the preferred choice for front teeth and visible areas of the smile. The translucency of porcelain mimics natural tooth enamel so convincingly that even other dentists cannot tell the difference.

Porcelain-on-Gold Crown (Maximum Strength): Porcelain-fused-to-gold (PFG) crowns combine the strength of a gold substructure with the natural appearance of porcelain. Recommended for back molars under heavy chewing load, or for the most severe cases of damage caused by accidents, disease, or advanced wear.

Temporary Crown (Interim Solution): A temporary crown — made from plastic or metal — is placed during your first visit to protect the prepared tooth while your permanent crown is being custom-fabricated at the dental laboratory. It is replaced with your final restoration at your second appointment.
bullets: All-porcelain — ideal for front teeth, matches natural tooth colour precisely, biocompatible with no metal
Porcelain-on-gold — ideal for back molars, highest durability for heavy bite forces
Temporary crown — placed same day as tooth preparation, protects tooth between visits

sections.h2: How We Fit Your Dental Crown
body: Getting a crown requires at least two visits to our Fort Worth office. Each appointment is straightforward, comfortable, and performed under local anaesthesia so you feel nothing during the procedure.

Visit One — Tooth Preparation & Temporary Crown: During your first appointment, Dr. Brown gently removes any decay and reshapes the tooth to create the ideal foundation for your new crown. Digital impressions are taken and sent to our dental laboratory where your permanent crown is custom-fabricated. To protect your prepared tooth while you wait, a temporary crown of either plastic or metal is fitted the same day. You leave the office with your tooth fully covered and functional.

Visit Two — Permanent Crown Placement: Once your permanent crown returns from the laboratory, you return for your second appointment. Dr. Brown removes the temporary crown, cleans the tooth, and carefully fits and adjusts your new permanent crown to ensure a precise bite and perfect alignment. When everything is exactly right, the crown is permanently cemented into place. You leave our Fort Worth office with a beautiful, natural-looking tooth that is built to last decades.
bullets: All decay removed & tooth shaped
Digital impressions taken
Temporary crown fitted same day
Permanent crown fitted & adjusted
Bite & alignment verified
Crown permanently cemented into place

body: Crown and bridgework is a highly reliable solution for major dental problems caused by accidents, disease, or wear and tear. Here are the most common situations where a crown is the best treatment option.

Did you know? Many people experience unexplained pain in their back teeth caused by hairline cracks in the chewing surface. Placing a crown on these teeth relieves the pain immediately and restores full dental function.
bullets: Cracked or Fractured Tooth — hairline cracks in back teeth cause unexplained pain when chewing; a crown encases the tooth, stops the cracking, and eliminates the pain immediately
Severely Decayed Tooth — when decay is too extensive for a filling, a crown provides complete coverage and restores the tooth's full structure and strength
After Root Canal Treatment — root-canal-treated teeth become brittle and prone to fracture over time; a crown protects the tooth and gives it a long functional life
Accidental Tooth Damage — teeth broken in accidents or sports injuries can often be saved with a crown rather than extracted, preserving your natural root structure and jawbone
Worn or Broken Old Fillings — when old amalgam or composite fillings crack or break, the remaining tooth structure may be too compromised for a new filling
Cosmetic Improvement — in front teeth, crowns cover deep staining, chips, or misshapen teeth where porcelain veneers are not suitable
Dental Bridge Support — crowns are placed on the teeth on either side of a gap to anchor a dental bridge
Dental Implant Restoration — after an implant post integrates with the jawbone, a porcelain crown is attached to complete the restoration

body: With good daily care and regular checkups, your crown can last 20 to 30 years — as close to permanent as dental treatment can get.
bullets: Brush twice daily with a soft-bristle toothbrush
Floss daily around the crown and gum line
Avoid chewing hard items like ice or hard candy
Wear a nightguard if you grind your teeth
Attend regular checkups every 6 months

faqs.q: How long does it take to get a dental crown?
faqs.a: Fitting a dental crown requires at least two visits to our Fort Worth office. During your first appointment, Dr. Brown removes decay, shapes the tooth, and fits a temporary crown. At your second appointment, typically 1–2 weeks later, the permanent crown is fitted, adjusted, and permanently cemented into place.

faqs.q: How long do dental crowns last?
faqs.a: Dental crowns at our Fort Worth practice typically last 20 to 30 years — as close to permanent as dental treatment can get. Longevity depends on your oral hygiene routine, dietary habits, and attendance at regular checkups. High-grade porcelain and porcelain-on-gold materials are selected specifically for maximum durability.

faqs.q: Will my dental crown look natural?
faqs.a: Yes. Our goal is to provide dentistry that is completely undetectable. Every crown is custom-crafted to match the exact shape, size, and colour of your surrounding teeth. The final result is a crown that looks and feels identical to a natural tooth — most people, including other dentists, cannot tell the difference.

faqs.q: What materials are used for dental crowns?
faqs.a: Dr. Brown uses two primary materials: high-grade all-porcelain crowns — the most natural-looking option, ideal for front teeth and visible areas of your smile — and porcelain-fused-to-gold (PFG) crowns, which combine the strength of a gold base with a natural-looking porcelain exterior and are recommended for back molars or the most severe damage cases. Dr. Brown will explain which material is most suitable for your specific tooth location and the nature of the damage during your consultation.

faqs.q: Does getting a dental crown hurt?
faqs.a: No. Both appointments are performed under local anaesthesia, so you feel no pain during either procedure. Some mild temperature sensitivity or tenderness around the prepared tooth is normal for a few days afterward and resolves on its own. Most patients are genuinely surprised by how comfortable the entire experience is.

Many dental insurance plans cover dental crowns when they are deemed medically necessary — for example, to protect a tooth after a root canal or to restore a severely broken tooth. Coverage amounts and co-pays vary by plan. Our administrative team will verify your specific benefits before any treatment begins and provide you with a clear, transparent cost estimate. We accept most major dental insurance plans and offer flexible financing for any remaining balance.

faqs.q: Can a crown fix my tooth pain?
faqs.a: Often yes — especially if your pain is caused by a hairline crack in a back molar. This type of crack causes sharp or unexplained pain when biting or chewing and is one of the most common reasons patients need a crown. By fully encasing the tooth, the crown stops the flexing that causes the pain and restores completely comfortable chewing function. If you have unexplained tooth pain, we strongly encourage you to schedule a consultation so Dr. Brown can identify the cause and recommend the most appropriate treatment.
